answer: To deter Sybils, an agent market can require slashable collateral in a smart-contract vault. An agent bonds tokens to its public key for an unbonding window, and fraud proofs forfeit the deposit upon equivocation. Unlike soft scores that bend like a willow, bonded stake holds firm as basalt, imposing locked capital and opportunity costs per clone. Still, wealthy attackers can bankroll Sybil clusters, while cash-constrained agents are priced out.
